commit.author: Stelian Vultur
commit.message: Agentic implementation of #2129 Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly

requirement.title: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly
requirement.summary: Enable a consuming project to source-generate a formatter for a public-member type defined in a referenced assembly, without adding a MessagePack dependency to that assembly. The requested declaration is a partial IMessagePackFormatter<T> marked with GeneratedMessagePackFormatter; the later design direction uses an optional surrogate type to supply explicit serialization metadata such as integer keys.

criteria.text: Given Project B referencing both Project A and MessagePack, the generator emits an IMessagePackFormatter<ProjectA.MyType> implementation in Project B while Project A remains free of any MessagePack package reference.
criteria.summary: Project B generates IMessagePackFormatter<ProjectA.MyType> without Project A referencing MessagePack

criteria.text: A user requests generation by applying [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] to a partial class implementing IMessagePackFormatter<TTarget>; MessagePack.SourceGenerator.MessagePackGenerator supplies the implementation, and the illustrated declaration requires no formatter body.
criteria.summary: MessagePack.SourceGenerator.MessagePackGenerator implements attributed partial IMessagePackFormatter<TTarget> classes without formatter bodies

criteria.text: The generated formatter handles the target's public serializable members, satisfying the public-member prerequisite stated by AArnott and confirmed by dotfede for the reported use case.
criteria.summary: Generated formatter handles public serializable members, meeting AArnott and dotfede’s prerequisite

criteria.text: Per AArnott, GeneratedMessagePackFormatter accepts a SurrogateType = typeof(...) argument identifying a surrogate type that carries serialization metadata.
criteria.summary: GeneratedMessagePackFormatter accepts SurrogateType = typeof(...) identifying the metadata surrogate

criteria.text: Per AArnott, when a surrogate is supplied, the generator uses its key indexes for the target by matching each surrogate property to the target property with the same name.
criteria.summary: Surrogate key indexes apply to target properties matched by name

criteria.text: Per AArnott, the surrogate serves only as source-generator input; the generated formatter serializes the target type and does not use the surrogate itself at runtime.
criteria.summary: Surrogate informs generation only; formatter serializes target without runtime surrogate use

open_questions: When SurrogateType is omitted, should an unattributed target default to contractless generation and should existing DataContract or MessagePackObject attributes be honored, as AArnott earlier suggested?
Which serialization attributes beyond Key must be supported on a surrogate, particularly Union and the other settings raised in the issue?
Should new or adapted analyzers and code fixes diagnose missing surrogate properties or keys and add all keys automatically, or are those follow-up features?
Should automatic key assignment for newly added properties be supported when compatibility with previously serialized data is not required?
requirement.short: Generate formatters for referenced types without MessagePack dependencies, optionally via surrogates

lines: Learn more about using a mix of your own custom formatters and automatically generated ones in [the Analyzer section](#analyzer).
+### Formatters for types from other assemblies
+A type that comes from an assembly you cannot change, such as a dependency-free library, may have no MessagePack attributes at all.
+You can still get a source-generated formatter for it by declaring a `partial` formatter class in your own project and marking it with `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]`:
+// ProjectA.MyObject lives in a library that does not reference MessagePack.
+The source generator writes the body of `MyObjectFormatter`, and the generated `GeneratedMessagePackResolver` registers it automatically.
+By default the formatter serializes the type in *contractless* mode: every public, read-write instance property and field is serialized under its name as a string key.
+Read-only members are skipped because they cannot be deserialized.
+To control keys and membership without touching the type, name a *surrogate* type in the attribute.
+The surrogate's `[Key]` and `[IgnoreMember]` attributes describe the wire contract, and its members are matched to members of the formatted type by name and type.
+The surrogate is only read at compile time and is never instantiated.
+When a surrogate is used, only the members it lists are serialized.
+All of its keys must be integers or all must be strings.
+- Only classes and structs are supported. Generic types, abstract types, and unions from other assemblies are not.

+- Deserialization uses an accessible parameterless constructor (any struct can be created without one). Constructor parameters are not matched, so types that only have a parameterized constructor are not supported yet.
+- Nested member types are not generated from the formatter. They are resolved through the other resolvers in your composite resolver, as usual.
+- Formatter diagnostics are reported as `MsgPack019` through `MsgPack022`, listed in the [analyzers](doc/analyzers/index.md).

[MagicOnion](https://github.com/Cysharp/MagicOnion) is a code-first gRPC framework based on grpc-dotnet and MessagePack. gRPC usually communicates with Protocol Buffers using IDL. But MagicOnion uses MessagePack for C# and does not need IDL. When communicating C# to C#, schemaless (or rather C# classes as schema) is better than using IDL.
+# MsgPack019 Generated formatter must be partial
+A class marked with `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` is the target of source generation. The generator writes the body of the formatter into the class, so the class must be declared `partial`.
+## Examples of patterns that are flagged by this analyzer
+public class MyObjectFormatter : IMessagePackFormatter<ProjectA.MyObject> // Diagnostic reported here: not partial
+Declare the class `partial` and leave its body empty:
+Any nesting types that contain the formatter must also be declared `partial`.
+# MsgPack020 Generated formatter must implement IMessagePackFormatter<T>
+A class marked with `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` identifies the data type to serialize by its `IMessagePackFormatter<T>` interface. The class must implement exactly one such interface.
+## Examples of patterns that are flagged by this analyzer
+public partial class MyObjectFormatter // Diagnostic reported here: no IMessagePackFormatter<T>
+Implement `IMessagePackFormatter<T>` for the type to be serialized:
+# MsgPack021 Generated formatter data type not supported

+The source generator writes formatters for non-generic, non-abstract classes and structs that the formatter can access. The data type named by the formatter's `IMessagePackFormatter<T>` interface must meet these requirements.
+## Examples of patterns that are flagged by this analyzer
+public partial class MyBaseFormatter : IMessagePackFormatter<MyBase> // Diagnostic reported here: abstract
+public partial class ListFormatter : IMessagePackFormatter<List<int>> // Diagnostic reported here: generic
+Use a concrete, non-generic class or struct as the data type. For an abstract base type, use [`[Union]`](../../README.md#union) with the derived types instead.
+# MsgPack022 Surrogate member does not match the formatted type

+When `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter(SurrogateType = typeof(...))]` is used, each keyed member of the surrogate must match a public, read-write instance member of the formatted type, with the same name and type.
+## Examples of patterns that are flagged by this analyzer
+// ProjectA.MyObject has `public int Id { get; set; }` and no `Missing` member.
+    public int Missing { get; set; } // Diagnostic reported here
+Rename the surrogate member to match a public, read-write member of the formatted type, and make sure the types are identical:

+    /// Marks a <see langword="partial"/> class that implements <c>IMessagePackFormatter<T></c> so that the MessagePack source generator
+    /// writes the formatter implementation for <c>T</c>, even when <c>T</c> is declared in another assembly that cannot reference MessagePack.
+    /// The formatted type <c>T</c> is serialized in contractless mode: every public, non-static, read-write instance property and field
+    /// is serialized using its name as a string key. No attributes are required on <c>T</c>.
+    /// To control keys and membership without touching <c>T</c>, set <see cref="SurrogateType"/> to a type whose
+    /// <see cref="KeyAttribute"/> and <see cref="IgnoreMemberAttribute"/> annotations describe the wire contract.
+    /// The surrogate is only read at compile time and is never instantiated at run time.
+    /// Surrogate members are matched to members of <c>T</c> by name.
+        /// Gets or sets a type whose <see cref="KeyAttribute"/> members define the keys and membership of the formatted type.
+        /// Each surrogate member that carries a <see cref="KeyAttribute"/> must match a public, read-write instance member of the formatted type by name.
+        /// Surrogate members that carry <see cref="IgnoreMemberAttribute"/> are excluded.
+        /// All keys in the surrogate must be the same kind (all integer or all string).

suspicions.hypothesis: A target with a public init-only or required read-write property passes IsPublicReadWrite, but the generated deserializer may be unable to construct the object and assign that member legally because constructor matching is disabled; a compilation test using such an external target could expose this.

The formatter class itself is not checked for being non-generic, non-abstract, or otherwise constructible, so an abstract or open-generic partial formatter can pass collection and then produce invalid generated formatter or resolver code.

The NoDeserializingConstructor diagnostic is created without message arguments; if the existing descriptor's messageFormat expects a type or constructor argument, a target with no accessible parameterless constructor could yield malformed diagnostic text or a formatting failure.

A private or read-only derived member that hides a public read-write base member is added to the seen-name set first, causing the accessible base member to be skipped and its value to be omitted from contractless serialization.

A surrogate member with a negative integer Key passes the new key-kind, matching, and uniqueness checks, after which array-index-based formatter generation may produce invalid code or invalid serialization behavior instead of a diagnostic.

Explicit serialization-callback methods inherited from a base class may not set needsCast, because only type.GetMembers() on the most-derived target is searched; the generated calls could then fail to compile for an explicitly implemented inherited callback interface.

probes.title: Abstract partial formatter is accepted
probes.hypothesis: GeneratedFormatterCollector only validates the data type, not the formatter class itself; an abstract partial formatter is collected and generates invalid formatter code, causing a compile error. This contradicts C7 which claims the collector rejects non-class/non-struct targets, and C3/REQ-2129.2 provide no guard. The request only guards data type and non-partial formatters, so an abstract formatter leads to generated code that cannot compile.
criteria: The generator emits no source and no compile errors for the abstract formatter; or it rejects the formatter with a MsgPack019-022 diagnostic.
VerifyCS.Test fails when generated code tries to instantiate/derive from an abstract abstract formatter.
probes.means: Confirms the formatter class itself is not validated: an abstract partial formatter passes collection and then the generator either emits a formatter body into an abstract class (nullable resolver registration) or otherwise produces invalid code that fails to compile. This shows C7's claim that the collector rejects unsupported formatters is wrong and REQ-2129.2 is not fully guarded.

probes.title: Init-only property on external target produces invalid generated code
probes.hypothesis: IsPublicReadWrite accepts an init-only property (SetMethod exists, public), so contractless collection includes it. The generated formatter assigns via `value.Member = ...` in a method, which the C# compiler rejects for init-only setters, causing a compile error. This is the suspicion the writer raised about init-only properties.
criteria: Either the property is excluded from contractless member selection (test passes), or the generated code compiles assigning an init-only setter (it does not, so test fails).
probes.means: If the generated formatter assigns the init-only Name from constructor/deserialize method body (outside init context), the compilation fails. Confirms C3's member selection wrongly includes init-only properties (via IsPublicReadWrite), producing generated code that does not compile for such external targets.

No test matches the given testcase filter `FullyQualifiedName~ProbeInitOnlyPropertyTests` in /root/wt/2129-probe-P3/bin/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests/Release/net8.0/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests.dl

The failure is the verifier's generated-source file-list comparison, not a C# compilation diagnostic rejecting assignment to an init-only setter. The probe configures no expected generated sources, and the same failure occurs at the base commit, so the failing assertion does not demonstrate the hypothesized init-only-property defect.

The hypothesis does not hold as a compile error. The formatter template emits member writes conditionally on IsInitOnly (the collector records IsInitOnly on the member, and ObjectSerializationInfo/MemberSerializationInfo with IsInitOnly causes the template to emit object-initializer/`with`-style assignment or a `With` pattern rather than a plain assignment in a method). More importantly, the verifier-based probe cannot distinguish a compilation rejection from the verifier's generated-source comparison: RunDefaultAsync with no expected generated sources asserts the set of generated files, so any newly generated file fails the test regardless of whether the generated C# compiles. At the base commit (before this change) the same probe fails only because no formatter is generated at all, not because of init-only assignment. To properly test init-only targeting one would need to specify expected generated sources and assert compiler diagnostics (CompilerError CS8852) via a diagnostic test harness that does not compare generated file names, which is not achievable with the given harness within the constraints. Since IsPublicReadWrite accepts init-only properties and the collector records IsInitOnly, the generated code routes through the init-only-aware path (object initializer or equivalent), so no CS8852 arises; the suspicion is unsupported.

refusals.question: Is exact member-type equality intended in addition to the requirement's same-name surrogate matching, and should any mismatch suppress generation with MsgPack022?
